podcasts.title: How Fast Should We Build Superintelligence? | Nick Bostrom
podcasts.description:
The question isn’t simply whether humanity should race toward superintelligence or stop. Nick Bostrom argues the harder challenge is preserving the ability to slow down when safety falls behind, without turning a temporary pause into permanent technological stagnation.

a16z’s Eddy Lazzarin and Elena Burger sit down with Bostrom to revisit the ideas he helped bring into the mainstream, now that increasingly capable AI systems actually exist. They discuss why alignment may become harder as models grow more situationally aware, which capability improvements may carry more risk than others, and why Bostrom favors “pacing the frontier” rather than committing to a broad or indefinite pause.

They also examine the cost of waiting. Bostrom argues that safely developed superintelligence could radically extend human lifespans and address problems from disease to poverty, meaning delay carries risks of its own. From there, the conversation turns to Deep Utopia, governance, the possibility of post-human forms of life, the simulation argument, and whether AI could eventually surpass humans at philosophy itself.

podcasts.title: Superintelligence Needs the Physical World with CEO and Co-Founder of Arda Bob McGrew
podcasts.description:
Is the AI singularity actually coming? Bob McGrew, former Chief Research Officer at OpenAI, argues that superintelligence won’t arrive without changes in the physical world, and that the “hard takeoff” argument is wrong.

Sarah Guo and Elad Gil sit down with Bob, an early key executive at Palantir who later led research at OpenAI. He is now CEO and co-founder of Arda, which is leveraging AI to make American manufacturing competitive. Bob explains why automating AI researchers is a one-time boost rather than a runaway loop, and why GPUs, compute, wet labs, and factories are the real bottlenecks. 

They cover Arda’s work with Anduril on everything from actuators to missiles to the Fury combat aircraft, why Arda is building “Cursor for manufacturing engineers”, and how the forward deployed engineering model really works. Plus, the big-picture future view: machines that make machines, self-replicating factories, and Bob’s answer to the Fermi paradox.

podcasts.title: 189: Geodesic顾全全：预训练有点“无聊”了，但用scaling改变AI制药才刚开始
podcasts.description:
「The best model is yet to come, scaling continues.（最好的模型尚未到来，规模化仍在继续。）」

今年 6 月 ，顾全全发推宣告离开字节，推文的最后一句如此写道。

这句话串起了他在字节 3 年多的工作：一是 AI 制药，他带团队做出了蛋白质结构预测模型 SeedFold 和蛋白质设计模型 SeedProteo；一是豆包的预训练，2025 年初，他的团队开始负责其中的 scaling 与优化部分。

不久后，我们在 6 月中旬于硅谷采访了顾全全，当时他正在筹备 AI 制药方向的创业。

今年 9 月，这家新公司 Geodesic Intelligence 亮相，发布了药物发现智能体平台 NovaDDE，以及 NovaAtom-Lite-Preview。11 月 10 日，Geodesic 又更新了全原子结构预测模型 今年确实有很多 AI 医疗的新公司出现，比如字节就有小荷健康。

顾全全的离职引起了一些争议。他自称字节 AI 制药负责人和 Seed 预训练的”优化与规模化“负责人（optimazation & scaling lead）。而此后有媒体的报道暗示，接近字节的人士并不认可这种表达。

我们在节目中直接讨论了：大公司如何组织不同方向的研究，为什么存在对 “负责人” 的不同定义。

顾全全说，离开的原因之一是 “有点儿无聊” 了。他认为预训练仍有大量要完善的细节和创新空间，但秘密正在减少，工程和组织能力在竞争中的比重越来越大。“方案很早就出现了，但团队要花几个月论证、形成共识，再推进。”

而 scaling 本身仍有巨大空间，“scaling continues” 就是新方向：把大模型上验证的 scaling 方法带进更多领域。

在顾全全眼中，AI 制药就是一个数据量巨大，但却仍未被 scaling 思路改造的富矿。他说这次创业，前六个月的算力花费就需要 1000 万美元。

与 Anthropic 的判断一致，顾全全也认为做 AI 制药必须自己掌握 “湿实验室”。因为从模型设计出候选分子到真的发现新药，还要通过湿实验来验证亲和力、成功率、毒性、可合成性和特异性……而实验结果又能作为奖励信号，进入模型后训练。

在顾全全离职前后，字节跳动还走出了数家 AI 制药公司，包括肖文之创立的 Molence Bio，以及在字节官方支持下独立融资，由刘凯创立的 Anew Labs。

本期，我们从顾全全离开字节聊起，拆解基模当下的 scaling 状态和预训练如何组织； AI for Science 能否出现一次类似 AI coding 的跃迁。最后，我们回到学界与工业界之间：当榜单把不同 “门派” 拉上同一擂台，什么才算有野心的研究？

本期嘉宾：
顾全全，Geodesic Intelligence 创始人
本期主播：
程曼祺，《晚点 LatePost》科技报道负责人

本期剪辑：吴宇量

Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic and former OpenAI research chief, warns that AI could create a country of geniuses inside a data center within just one to five years, triggering unprecedented disruption to employment, national security and democracy. He explains how AI could eliminate entry-level jobs in software engineering, law, finance and consulting, potentially wiping out half of white-collar entry-level positions and pushing unemployment to 10–20%. He warns that autonomous drone swarms, mass surveillance and increasingly independent AI agents could undermine constitutional protections and human control. Amodei calls for international agreements to prevent AI-powered biological weapons and argues that controlling advanced AI is a complex engineering challenge, while admitting that dangerous failures are inevitable if development continues this quickly.

podcasts.title: Software engineering after code becomes cheap with Satya Nadella
podcasts.description:
What does software engineering look like when generating code becomes cheap, and verifying it becomes the hard part? With Satya Nadella, Microsoft’s CEO, who is one of the very few Big Tech CEOs who started his career as a software engineer (back at Sun Microsystems). He joins me to discuss how building software is changing inside Microsoft, and what these changes mean for engineers.

—
*Brought to you by:*
• turbopuffer – a vector and full-text search engine built on object storage. It’s fast, cheap, and extremely scalable. https://turbopuffer.com/pragmatic
• Linear – the product development system for teams and agents. https://linear.app/pragmatic
• WorkOS – everything you need to make your app enterprise ready. https://workos.com/

—

Sidenote: we recorded this episode in Redmond just a few hours before Microsoft’s day-long Outlook outage, so there was no discussion of it. I am already talking with the team inside Microsoft on-point for this outage, and expect a more detailed follow-up in the newsletter on what went wrong and what we can learn from it.
 
—

podcasts.title: Ep. 044 - Is NVIDIA Over? Emergency Pod with ChinaTalk | Dylan Patel, Jordan Nanos, Jordan Schneider (ChinaTalk)
podcasts.description:
Emergency pod. Hours after NVIDIA announced that Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO, with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO, Jordan Nanos (@JordanNanos) sits down with Dylan Patel (@dylan522p) and ChinaTalk's Jordan Schneider (@jordanschnyc). They get into why the MATCH Act matters more than RASA, how much compute China should be allowed to rent abroad, the smuggling cases around NVIDIA's supply chain, China's push onto domestic accelerators, whether NVIDIA can execute without its founder, and who should run it next. Then it goes off the rails.


Read the article: https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/nvidia-and-the-world-without-jensen
